objective: G18 with G17. For the seven-knot structure and every structure of the smallest-structure census, decide by exhaustive census of founder sets whether ordinary growth reaches its old part from a proper part of it, and give the reason where it cannot. Stop at a founder set that reaches one, or the reasons for all.
status: Computed with one counting argument, referee pending. Ordinary growth changes how much each old word counts and never which are allowed (0 changes in 17.6 million grown tables). The seven-knot structure is not reached from any of its 19 founder starts (24 to 48 observer words against 16). In 34 histories a start with hidden score at most 2 gains a hidden excess at round 1 (smallest: 7 knots at exactly 2, one not-all-equal birth on two loose distinctions, 55/27); every such start has a distinction held three times. Among the 12,147 starts with at most two holders none gains one. One settled statement of the pre-registration was false (a newborn's parity sign is not a renaming after the next round); both versions give the same verdicts.
title: Can ordinary growth with both laws reach the structures with a hidden excess?
